submission.purposeContent2: Submissions may be based on research work or surgical video material. After initial review by the Scientific Committee, selected finalists will enter the same on-site final competition. All finalists will follow the same presentation format: an 8-minute presentation followed by 2 minutes of Q&A.
submission.purposeContent1: The TSESS 2026 Best Endoscopic Presentation Competition aims to encourage clinical research, technical innovation, surgical education, and case experience exchange in the field of endoscopic spine surgery. Awards are not based on submission format but on the overall contribution of the work to the field of endoscopic spine surgery.
submission.researchPresentationContent: Clinical research, basic science research, technical research, systematic review, case series, educational research or other work relevant to endoscopic spine surgery.
submission.surgicalVideoContent1: Endoscopic decompression, endoscopic fusion, navigation / robotics, complication management, innovative techniques, difficult case management or educational demonstration.
submission.surgicalVideoContent2: Surgical video submissions are not intended to be simple video playback. Finalists must deliver an 8-minute slide-based presentation and incorporate selected video clips to explain the clinical problem, technical concept, imaging interpretation, surgical steps and educational value.
submission.initialReviewDetail: Scientific Committee review and finalist selection
submission.notificationDetail: Acceptance, finalist status and presentation details announced
submission.finalCompetitionDetail: On-site presentations, judging and award ceremony
submission.eligibility1: Presenting authors must complete TSESS 2026 meeting registration. Non-members may submit after completing meeting registration.
submission.eligibility2: Each submission may have only one presenting author. The presenting author should generally be the first author. Any change of presenting author must be requested by November 25, 2026 and approved by the organizer.
submission.eligibility3: Each first author may submit up to 3 works.
submission.eligibility4: Submitted work must have a clear relationship to endoscopic spine surgery, including education, technique, clinical application, complication management, patient safety, image guidance, device development or related topics.
submission.eligibility5: Failure to attend the on-site presentation will be regarded as withdrawal from presentation and competition.
submission.abstractRequirement1: All submissions must include an English abstract. The abstract is limited to 400 words, excluding title, author names and affiliations.
submission.abstractRequirement2: Research abstracts should include Purpose, Materials and Methods, Results and Conclusion. Surgical video abstracts should include Background, Technique, Clinical Relevance and Educational Value.
submission.abstractRequirement3: Figures, tables, references and keywords should not be included in the abstract. The title should clearly reflect the topic. Abbreviations must be defined at first use. Product names, if used, should be marked according to applicable trademark requirements.
submission.abstractRequirement4: Clinical studies should provide an IRB / REC approval number or exemption statement. If the work is exempt from IRB review according to institutional policy, this should be stated in the submission system. Authors using surgical video, clinical images or patient data must confirm that all necessary institutional permission or patient consent has been obtained.
submission.videoPrivacyTitle: 6. Surgical Video and Patient Privacy Requirements
submission.videoPrivacy1: Video clips should be used for education and technical explanation and must be integrated into the finalist's oral presentation.
submission.videoPrivacy2: Recommended video format: MP4, H.264, 1920 x 1080, 30 fps. Recommended file size: no more than 500 MB.
submission.videoPrivacy3: Videos and slides must not contain identifiable patient information, including name, medical record number, date of birth, face, tattoo or other unique identifiers.
submission.videoPrivacy4: Authors should avoid showing non-deidentified imaging data, examination forms, orders, hospital system screenshots or any information that may allow patient identification.
submission.videoPrivacy5: Use of patient surgical video, clinical photographs or imaging data must comply with the author's institutional requirements for patient consent or authorization. Authors must confirm this during submission, and the organizer may request supporting documentation if needed.
submission.coiContent1: All authors must disclose potential conflicts of interest, including but not limited to consulting fees, speaker fees, research funding, equity, patents, royalties, device or software support and any other relationships that may influence interpretation of the work. Authors with no conflict of interest should state "Nothing to disclose."
submission.coiContent2: This competition adopts a disclosure-based policy rather than an exclusion-based policy. Work previously presented at domestic or international meetings, submitted to journals, published, or submitted as an encore abstract may be considered. Authors must disclose prior meeting presentations, journal submission or publication status and relevant citations or sources. The Scientific Committee may consider these disclosures during review, selection or scoring.
submission.coiContent3: The first slide of the finalist presentation must be a COI disclosure slide.
submission.finalCompetitionTitle: 8. Initial Review and Final Competition Format
submission.finalCompetitionContent1: The Scientific Committee will review submissions based on innovation, academic or educational value, clinical impact, technical quality and overall presentation potential. Selected works will be invited to the on-site final competition.
submission.finalCompetitionContent2: The final competition will be conducted as one unified competition without separate research and video award tracks. All finalists will deliver an 8-minute presentation followed by 2 minutes of Q&A. Surgical video finalists must use slides with selected video clips for explanation; simple video playback without structured presentation will not be accepted.
submission.finalCompetitionContent3: Final slides must be prepared and presented in English using the official 16:9 slide template. Finalists must upload final slides and required video clips by November 25, 2026, 23:59. The organizer may require all files to be preloaded on the venue computer to keep the session on schedule.
submission.judgingDescription1: The final competition will be judged by 5 judges.
submission.judgingDescription2: Judges from the same institution as the presenter, with direct collaborative relationships, or with clear conflicts of interest should recuse themselves from scoring that presentation or be replaced by the organizer.
submission.innovationDescription: Novelty, technical advancement and importance of the research question
submission.academicValueDescription: Methodological quality, knowledge translation, teaching clarity and learnability
submission.clinicalImpactDescription: Impact on patient care, surgical safety, decision-making or clinical practice
submission.technicalQualityDescription: Surgical technique, image quality, data completeness, analytic accuracy and demonstration of safety boundaries
submission.presentationDescription: Time control, English delivery, slide structure and response to questions
submission.judgingDescription3: For each presentation, the highest and lowest judge scores will be removed. The final score will be the average of the remaining 3 judge scores. In the event of a tie, the judging panel may determine the final ranking based on clinical impact, innovation and panel discussion.
submission.awardsDescription: Awardees will be announced and recognized after the final competition on December 5, 2026. The organizer reserves the right to adjust award presentation according to submission quality and judges' decision.
submission.authorizationContent1: Abstracts may be modified online before the submission deadline. For accepted or finalist submissions, requests to modify title, author order, presenting author or content should be sent to the TSESS 2026 Secretariat within 7 days after notification.
submission.authorizationContent2: Withdrawal should be submitted in writing or by email before November 25, 2026 to allow program adjustment. Late withdrawal or absence from presentation may result in cancellation of presentation and competition eligibility.
submission.authorizationContent3: By submitting, authors confirm that the information is accurate, that all necessary co-author approvals, IRB / REC approvals or exemptions, patient consent or institutional authorization have been obtained, and that TSESS 2026 may use submitted abstracts, slides, video clips and meeting records for program book publication, website announcement, on-site presentation, post-meeting documentation and educational purposes.
submission.authorizationContent4: TSESS 2026 reserves the right to modify the rules, program arrangements and competition guidelines. Any unresolved matter or dispute shall be subject to the final announcement of TSESS 2026 and the decision of the Scientific Committee.
